newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Congress sessions end, budget unresolved.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Congress sessions end, budget unresolved.

text.p: Both houses of the Philippine Congress cut short a two-day special session on Monday, leaving an impasse over the 1997 budget still unresolved, officials in the two bodies said.

The two houses were to have held special sessions on Monday and Tuesday on a request from President Fidel Ramos. But the Senate and the House of Representatives decided to adjourn after they passed two special appropriation bills, the officials said.
Both houses approved a bill on salary increases for government employees worth 27 billion pesos and an additional internal revenue allocation of local government units for 14 billion pesos.

"We're still hoping for a possible compromise," said Senate President Ernesto Maceda, adding that the two wings of Congress would meet informally so there could be an agreement before regular sessions resume on January 20.

"We will not be able to approve the budget in two days. So we will only be able to approve the two bills to ensure that salary increases will be granted by January 1 and that increases in the internal revenue allocation will be approved," Ernesto Herrera, the Senate Finance Committee chairman, said earlier.
"Somebody will have to blink first," he said, adding that the House would have to agree to a cut in the countrywide development fund (CDF), which has divided the two sides.

The deadlock occurred after the opposition-dominated Senate slashed the CDF by 40 percent to 720 million pesos. Senators said they feared the administration-backed House would use the fund for early campaigning ahead of the presidential and congressional elections in May 1998.
House members have said the Senate does not have the constitutional right to amend its proposals.

Failure of the special sessions to pass the 1997 budget will not paralyse the operations of the government. Under Philippine law, it can draw money on the basis of the previous budget until Congress approves a new one.
But provisions for the CDF and other special funds will not be covered under the old budget, for which an agreement between the two wings of Congress will be needed.
